Materializing moltis from local mirror...

Analyzing moltis AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
```
prepare() {
    cd "${srcdir}/${pkgname}"
    
    # Increase recursion limit for all crate roots
    for f in crates/*/src/lib.rs crates/*/src/main.rs; do
        sed -i '/recursion_limit/d' "$f"
        echo '#![recursion_limit = "2048"]' | cat - "$f" > temp && mv temp "$f"
    done

    # Disable matrix feature globally as it causes build failure on stable Rust
    find . -name "Cargo.toml" -exec sed -i 's/"matrix",//g' {} +
    find . -name "Cargo.toml" -exec sed -i 's/"moltis-matrix\/metrics",//g' {} +

    export RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable
    cargo fetch --locked --target host-tuple
}

build() {
    cd "${srcdir}/${pkgname}/"

    export RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable
    export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target
    export LIBSQLITE3_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG=1
    export OPENSSL_NO_VENDOR=1
    export ZSTD_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG=1
    
    # Build web UI assets
    just build-web-assets
    
    # Build release binary
    cargo build --release --frozen -p moltis --features full
}

# check() {
#     cd "${srcdir}/${pkgname}/\\"
#
#     export RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable
#     cargo test --all-features
# }

package() {
    cd "${srcdir}/${pkgname}/\\"

    install -Dm0755 target/release/moltis -t "${pkgdir}/usr/bin/\\"
    install -Dm0644 README.md -t "${pkgdir}/usr/share/doc/${pkgname}"
    install -Dm0644 LICENSE.md -t "${pkgdir}/usr/share/licenses/${pkgname}/\\"
}
```

The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the PKGBUILD file to extract metadata, which means only global-level declarations are evaluated. All executable code is contained within function definitions (`prepare()`, `build()`, `package()`) that remain unexecuted during this phase. The global scope consists exclusively of standard variable assignments like `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `depends`, and `source` - no command substitutions, network downloads, or system modifications occur at this level. The file follows conventional PKGBUILD structure with legitimate build orchestration, so there's no malicious behavior activated by sourcing.
